title: Plain-language copy for the whole site, checked by Limatus and a jargon test
description: The site used builder jargon (engine, floor, cue, excess, trope, twin) a reader could not follow. Rewrite all public copy in plain language, set up Limatus from the Anth.us profile, and fail the build on jargon.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Plain-language copy
  Scenario: A first-time visitor can follow every page
    Given a reader who has never heard of this project
    When they read a page
    Then no sentence needs a term the page has not defined
  Scenario: Jargon cannot return
    Given the built site
    When npm test runs
    Then it fails on any banned word in visible text, alt text or previews

comments.author: home
comments.text: Shipped in 578a5fd: five writers rewrote page templates, characteristic and result pages, sentence builders, data descriptions and compliance guidance; jargon test is in npm test (0 banned words, was 33 kinds); Limatus profile, samples and scan in writing/. Follow-ups: repeated lead paragraph on one-model pages, heading 'phrase we added' on name-change results, Limatus repetition findings.

right_now_summary: Five writers rewrote the site in plain language, added a jargon test, and set up Limatus checks.
